newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ARSENAL STEP UP TITLE CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARSENAL STEP UP TITLE CHALLENGE.

text.p: Dennis Bergkamp scored once and set up a goal for Paul Merson on Sunday as Arsenal stepped up their premier league title challenge with a 3-1 win over Everton.

Dutch Bergkamp, who now starts a three-match ban, and French midfielder Patrick Viera scored in the space of two minutes 10 minutes after the interval with Merson scoring the third after Bergkamp had split open the Everton defence.
Everton scored a last-minute goal through Duncan Ferguson who soared high above the Arsenal defence to beat England goalkeeper David Seaman with a header.
Striker Ian Wright, returning after a three-match suspension, played the first half only before he was taken off as a precaution after sustaining a hamstring strain.
Arsenal's win consolidated third place in the league behind Liverpool and Manchester United who both won on Saturday.
Their north London rivals Tottenham Hotspur lost 2-1 at Nottingham Forest with Brian Roy scoring twice for the home side after Andy Sinton had given the Tottenham the lead after just 75 seconds.
Tottenham were reduced to 10 men when Swiss Ramon Vega was sent off at the end of the first half in only his second match for the club.
In the first division Queen's Park Rangers recovered from 4-0 down to draw 4-4 with Port Vale in a thrilling match at Vale Park.
QPR scored three goals in the final five minutes with John Spencer grabbing the equaliser in injury time.
